I agree with @Atko. Many times, I see people replying to trolls and it makes me face palm — many trolls do what they do in exchange for attention. Giving them any attention will just keep them around. No matter how badly you want to respond, learn to move on and ignore it. I group those who reply to trolls with the trolls themselves.

Other than that, I don't believe trolls deserve our time to deal with them in any extreme measures.

In theory I like the idea, but I think in practice... Not so much. The issue is that once enough people have banned a person there won't be anyone reporting that user for SPAM, breaking the rules, etc. This could turn out badly if someone becomes shadow banned and then starts posting really bad content.

I think a report button would work well if it also had the ability to block someone AFTER reporting them for spam, harassment, or breaking rules. That way a person would be blocked, and if enough people report/block them their account would have to be reviewed or something.

There are those who simply troll either for enjoyment or because they're being paid. Some are skilled enough to never 'break' any of the rules, but go out of their way to get as close to the line as possible.

I'd like to have the option to 'opt-out' of any further discussion for those specific individuals even if no rules were broken. I doubt we'll have a situation where everyone blocks one person, and they start spamming.

Or you could pull your head out of the sand and embrace the world as a much bigger and scarier place than you want to believe, but by embracing the bigger and scarier world you will grow as a human being. Be careful though. Seeing words you don't want to see and experiencing thoughts you don't want to think, may turn you into a person you didn't imagine possible. You will be forced to discipline yourself and look away from words and ideas you cannot change, ignore noise you cannot understand, concede debates you cannot win, and - gasp - contribute something new and meaningful to the world.
